questions.question: Which of the following best matches the textbook definition of a relation?
questions.explanation: The excerpt defines a relation as a set of ordered pairs (Definition 1.1).

questions.question: For the point P(3,2) in the text, which terms correctly name 3 and 2?
options: 3 is the abscissa and 2 is the ordinate.
3 is the ordinate and 2 is the abscissa.
3 is the origin and 2 is the ordinate.
3 is the x-intercept and 2 is the y-intercept.
questions.answer: 3 is the abscissa and 2 is the ordinate.
questions.explanation: The excerpt explains the first coordinate is the abscissa and the second is the ordinate (section 1.1.2, example P(3,2)).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What are the coordinates of the origin as given in the text?
questions.explanation: The excerpt states the origin has coordinates (0, 0) (section 1.1.2).

questions.question: According to the textbook convention, which axis is usually horizontal and oriented to the right?

questions.question: What is the next number in the sequence 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, ___ shown in Activity 1.1?

questions.question: Which statement matches the textbook definition of a function?
options: No two distinct ordered pairs have the same first element.
A function always maps multiple outputs to one input.
A function is any graph on the plane.
questions.answer: No two distinct ordered pairs have the same first element.
questions.explanation: Definition 1.3 in the excerpt states a function is a relation in which no two distinct ordered pairs have the same first element.
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Given the list (2,4), (4,3), (3,9), (18,−3), (9,3), (7,7), (3,12), (6,18), (30,5), which ordered pairs does the excerpt state belong to the relation 'y is a multiple of x' (Example 2)?
questions.explanation: Example 2 lists those five ordered pairs as belonging to the relation where the second is a multiple of the first (section 'Example 2').

questions.question: Which sentence correctly states the Vertical Line Test as given in the text?
options: A numerical relation is a function iff no vertical line intersects its graph in more than one point.
A graph is a function iff it is symmetric about the y-axis.
A relation is a function iff it has equal domain and range.
A graph is a function iff every horizontal line intersects it at most once.
questions.answer: A numerical relation is a function iff no vertical line intersects its graph in more than one point.
questions.explanation: The excerpt explicitly states a numerical relation is a function iff no vertical line intersects the graph in more than one point (Vertical Line Test note).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Why does the excerpt show f(x)=3x+5 is one-to-one?
options: Because f(a)=f(b) leads to 3a+5=3b+5 and so a=b.
Because its graph is a parabola.
Because its range is non-negative only.
questions.answer: Because f(a)=f(b) leads to 3a+5=3b+5 and so a=b.
questions.explanation: Example 1 under One-to-one demonstrates f( )=3 +5 is one-to-one by showing f(1)=f(2) implies 3·1+5=3·2+5, hence 1=2, so in general f(a)=f(b) ⇒ a=b (section 1.2.3).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: According to the textbook, which statement about f(x)=2 is correct?
questions.explanation: The excerpt states when a=0 in f(x)=ax+b the function reduces to f(x)=b which is called a constant function, and example 3 shows f(x)=2 as a constant function (section 'Graph of linear function').
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: For the linear function f(x)=3x−6 stated in the examples, what are the x- and y-intercepts?
questions.explanation: The excerpt finds the x-intercept by setting f(x)=0 giving x=2, and the y-intercept by setting x=0 giving f(0)=−6 (section 'Example 1' under Slope and intercept).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What is the vertex of the quadratic function f(x)=x^2+6x+11 after completing the square as shown in the text?
questions.explanation: The excerpt completes the square: x^2+6x+11 = (x+3)^2 + 2, so the vertex is (−3,2) (section 'Example 1' in completing the square).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: For the curve y=(x−3)^2+2 discussed in the text, what is its y-intercept?
questions.explanation: Setting x=0 gives y=(0−3)^2+2=9+2=11, so the y-intercept is 11 as shown in the example (section 'Example 1' under 'Graph of y=a(x−k)^2 + c').
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: What is the maximum value of f(x)=−(x−3)^2+1 as found in the text?
questions.explanation: The excerpt writes f(x)=−(x−3)^2+1 and notes the vertex (3,1) gives the maximum value 1 because the parabola opens downward (Example 2 under Minimum and Maximum values).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Which are the solutions (x values) of x^2−4=0 as obtained graphically in the examples?

questions.question: From the worked example, the solution set of x^2−6x+8<0 is which interval?
questions.explanation: The example solving x^2−6x+8<0 finds the parabola is below the x-axis between the roots x=2 and x=4, so the solution is (2,4) (section 'Example 1' under 'Graphical method of solving quadratic inequalities').

questions.question: What is the domain of f(x)=√(x−2) as shown in the excerpt?
questions.explanation: The excerpt states for f(x)=√(x−2) the expression under the radical must be non-negative, so x−2 ≥ 0 and domain is x ≥ 2 (Example under 'If f(x)=√(x−2)').

questions.question: Using examples in the text, (f+g)(x) is defined as which expression when f and g have overlapping domains?

questions.question: Demonstrate in one algebraic step why f(x)=3x+5 is one-to-one as shown in the text.
questions.answer: If f(a)=f(b) then 3a+5=3b+5, which implies a=b.
questions.explanation: The excerpt shows that equating f(a) and f(b) leads to 3a+5=3b+5 and cancellation yields a=b, proving injectivity (section 'Example 1' under One-to-one function).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.topic: Domain and range of linear function
questions.question: State the domain and range of f(x)=3x+5 as given in the examples.
questions.answer: Domain = all real numbers; Range = all real numbers.
questions.explanation: The excerpt explains f(x)=3x+5 is defined for every real x, so both domain and range are the set of all real numbers (section 'Example 2' under 'For each of the following functions').
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.topic: Domain and range of radical function
questions.question: For f(x)=√(x−2) given in the text, what are the domain and range?
questions.explanation: The excerpt requires the expression under the radical to be non-negative so x−2 ≥ 0 (domain x ≥ 2), and square root values are ≥ 0 (range y ≥ 0) (Example under functions).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Complete the square for f(x)=x^2+6x+11 and state the vertex (as done in the text).
questions.explanation: The excerpt completes the square: x^2+6x+11=(x+3)^2+2 and identifies the vertex (−3,2) (Example in completing the square section).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Using the example where f(x)=2x+4 and g(x)=3x−1, what is (f+g)(2)?
questions.explanation: The excerpt computes (f+g)(x)=(2x+4)+(3x−1)=5x+3 and then (f+g)(2)=5(2)+3=13 (example in Sum of functions).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Given f(x)=x^2+1 and g(x)=x^2+2x−1 from the difference example, what is (f−g)(2)?
questions.explanation: The excerpt finds (f−g)(x)=(x^2+1)−(x^2+2x−1)=−2x+2 and evaluates at x=2 to get −4+2=−2 (Difference example solution).
questions.sourceNote: Grade 10 Mathematics Student Textbook, Unit 1: Relations and Functions (owner-connected Google Drive file 1MR1DGORWmpf10Z6KiVkMm04CxfgDQ0C8).

questions.question: Using the linear relation Height = 2.47·(femur length) + 54 from the example, what approximate height does the text compute for a femur of 44 cm?
questions.explanation: The excerpt computes Height = 2.47(44)+54 = 162.68 and states the woman is approximately 163 cm tall (Application example 1).

questions.question: Using the same relation Height = 2.47·(femur length) + 54, what approximate height does the excerpt compute for a femur of 51 cm?
